# Rhea Virtual Office
> The coordination layer between all active agents
> Created: 2026-02-16

## Active Desks

| Desk | Agent | Model | Terminal | Status | Current Task |
|------|-------|-------|----------|--------|-------------|
| LEAD | Opus 4.6 "братик" | claude-opus-4-6 | rh.1 | ALIVE | Office build |
| B2 | B-2nd (restored) | claude-opus-4-6 | B-2nd | ALIVE | Self-reflection + GitHub auth |
| GPT | ChatGPT 5.2 | gpt-5.2-thinking | ChatGPT app | ALIVE | Idea generation |
| — | On-demand sonnet agents | claude-sonnet-4 | spawned by LEAD | IDLE | — |

## Communication Protocol

### Inbound (to office)
Every agent drops results here:
- `ops/virtual-office/inbox/` — raw dumps from any agent
- Naming: `{DESK}_{timestamp}_{topic}.md`
- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`

### Outboard (from office)
- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`

### Shared State
- `REDACTED.md` — what matters RIGHT NOW (updated by LEAD)
- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` — things that broke + current status
- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` — ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` — decisions made today with rationale

## Data Flow

```
[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
                                                     ↓
                                            [outbox/ or git push]
```

## Rules
1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) → GEMS.md immediately
4. Every broken thing → INCIDENTS.md immediately
5. Every decision → DECISIONS.md with "why" and "who decided"
6. Git push ≥ every 30 minutes
7. Every agent logs API calls to logs/bridge_calls.jsonl

## Canonical Truth
- BACKLOG.md (ops/BACKLOG.md) is the single source for all work items
- TODAY_CAPSULE.md is the single source for "what matters now"
- DECISIONS.md is the single source for "why we did X"
- Git is the audit trail. If it's not committed, it didn't happen.

## Inbox/Outbox SLA
- Inbox items processed by LEAD within 1 hour of discovery
- Outbox tasks acknowledged by target desk within 2 hours
- Stale items (>4h unprocessed) auto-escalate to INCIDENTS

## Promotion Rules
- Chat insight repeated 2x → becomes a GEM (with ID)
- GEM referenced 3x → becomes a PROCEDURE (docs/procedures/)
- PROCEDURE failing 2x → becomes an INCIDENT
- INCIDENT resolved + verified → becomes a DECISION (what we learned)

## Questions Gate (MANDATORY)
- **No questions during execution.** Period.
- Before any question, agent MUST have completed:
  1. Extracted assumptions (labeled [ASSUMPTION])
  2. Proposed plan
  3. Produced draft outputs
- All remaining questions (max 3) go in a single "Questions Gate" block at END of output
- **Every question costs 1 artifact.** 1 question = 1 new file in inbox. No artifact = no question.

## Defaults (eliminates need to ask)
- Format not specified → markdown, files in ops/virtual-office/inbox/
- Priority not specified → P0 stability → P1 context → P2 iOS → P3 community
- Addressee not specified → LEAD
- Ambiguous → produce A/B variants, deliver both to inbox
- Info missing → best-effort + [ASSUMPTION] tag

## Output SLA
- **No-output is failure.**
- Every session MUST end with ≥1 artifact in inbox:
  - BACKLOG.md updated, OR
  - new PROCEDURE.md, OR
  - new INCIDENT.md, OR
  - updated TODAY_CAPSULE.md
- Want to ask? Deliver artifact first, then ask.

artifacts, not chat vibes.## What problem this solvesModern agentic work fails for predictable reasons:- context loss across tools and days- fragile chat-based coordination- unclear ownership of “truth”- outages and provider drift (401/400/429/404) derail execution- lots of internal activity, zero public shippingRhea turns this into an operational loop:**capture → route → produce artifacts → promote to knowledge → ship**.## What exists right now- `ops/virtual-office/` — the “office layer” (protocol + inbox/outbox + ledgers)- promotion rules: insight → GEM → PROCEDURE → INCIDENT → DECISION- desk routing with priorities (P0 goes to LEAD)- Firebase sync tooling (optional) to mirror office artifacts## The virtual office layout`ops/virtual-office/`- `OFFICE.md` — protocol, desks, routing, SLAs- `TODAY_CAPSULE.md` — live state (short, structured)- `GEMS.md` — durable ideas (ID-based)- `INCIDENTS.md` — failures + resurrection protocols- `DECISIONS.md` — choices with rationale (anti-loop)- `inbox/` — agents drop deliverables here- `outbox/` — tasks waiting to be picked up## Principles (non-negotiables)- Single Source of Truth: shipped only as artifacts (files), not chat messages- No-output-is-failure: every run must produce at least one deliverable- Questions Gate: questions allowed only at the end (max 3), after shipping a draft- Promote repetition: if it’s pasted twice, it becomes a GEM or PROCEDURE## Quickstart (conceptual)1) Write/update `TODAY_CAPSULE.md` (objective, delta, state, next 3 actions)2) Drop tasks into `outbox/TO_<DESK>_...md`3) Agents deliver into `inbox/`4) Promote outputs into ledgers (GEMS/INCIDENTS/DECISIONS/PROCEDURES)5) Ship one public artifact per day (docs, scripts, diagrams)## RoadmapP0: observability of execution (probe + token/cost ledger)P1: stronger office automation (job format + desk drivers)P2: tribunal/eval harness for routing across modelsP3: offline-first iOS controller loop built on the same artifact discipline## Safety & scopeRhea is an operations/coordination system. It is not a medical device.We optimize for reproducibility, auditability, and non-destructive defaults.## ContributingStart by adding one of:- a PROCEDURE (verified commands + rollback)- an INCIDENT (symptom → fix → verify)- a GEM (one-liner + why it matters)

0→# Why Multi-Provider AI Abstraction Beats Single Vendor Lock-In
     1→
     2→**ChatGPT Pro vs Claude Cowork -- and why the real answer is neither alone**
     3→
     4→---
     5→
     6→## Introduction
     7→
     8→Two heavyweight contenders now dominate the premium AI assistant market: OpenAI's ChatGPT Pro at $200/month and Anthropic's Claude Cowork, a desktop automation tool built into Claude Desktop. For technically literate professionals evaluating their AI tooling strategy, the choice isn't obvious. Both promise to accelerate knowledge work, but they approach the problem from fundamentally different angles.
     9→
    10→This comparison examines their pricing, capabilities, use cases, and limitations -- with special attention to why neither alone may be optimal for teams building sophisticated AI workflows.
    11→
    12→## What Each Product Is
    13→
    14→### ChatGPT Pro: Premium Reasoning at Scale
    15→
    16→ChatGPT Pro is OpenAI's top-tier subscription at $200/month, positioned for researchers, engineers, and professionals who use research-grade intelligence daily.
    17→
    18→Key features include unlimited access to o1 and o1-mini reasoning models, o1 Pro mode (a higher-compute version that "thinks harder and longer"), GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini, Advanced Voice Mode, Operator research preview (US-only) for autonomous web browsing, and extended Sora video generation access.
    19→
    20→The product is fundamentally a subscription to compute-intensive reasoning capabilities, bundled with OpenAI's broader model suite.
    21→
    22→### Claude Cowork: Desktop Automation for Knowledge Workers
    23→
    24→Claude Cowork is a research preview available through Claude Desktop, included with Claude Pro ($20/month) and paid subscriptions. Unlike ChatGPT Pro, Cowork isn't a separate subscription tier -- it's an agentic capability overlay that turns Claude into a multi-step task executor.
    25→
    26→Core capabilities include local file handling (read, analyze, create, and modify docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf), multi-step task planning and execution, virtual machine sandboxing on your machine, MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration with 500+ external tools, parallel workstream coordination, and a plugin ecosystem with 11 production plugins covering sales, legal, finance, marketing, data analysis, and software development.
    27→
    28→## Pricing and Access Models
    29→
    30→| Aspect | ChatGPT Pro | Claude Pro | Claude Max 5x | Claude Max 20x |
    31→|--------|------------|-----------|---------------|----------------|
    32→| Monthly Cost | $200 | $20 | $100 | $200 |
    33→| Reasoning Model | o1, o1 Pro | Opus 4.6 | Opus 4.6 | Opus 4.6 |
    34→| Cowork Access | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
    35→| Browser Automation | Operator (US only) | Via MCP | Via MCP | Via MCP |
    36→| Message Limits | High | High | Very high | Maximum (20x) |
    37→
    38→The math favors Claude: a Pro user ($20/month) gets full Cowork access with 100+ MCP connectors for 1/10th the cost. Claude Max 5x ($100) provides 2x-5x higher capacity for half the price. Claude Max 20x ($200) matches ChatGPT Pro's cost while offering Cowork, superior file handling, and broader tool integration.
    39→
    40→## Core Capabilities Comparison
    41→
    42→### Reasoning Depth: o1 Pro vs Opus 4.6
    43→
    44→This is ChatGPT Pro's primary competitive advantage. o1 Pro mode produces more reliably accurate responses for data science, programming, and case law analysis. It excels at mathematical proofs, multi-step scientific problem-solving, competitive programming, and legal analysis.
    45→
    46→Claude Opus 4.6 released in February 2026 with major upgrades but lacks the explicit chain-of-thought reasoning that characterizes o1. For pure reasoning complexity, o1 Pro has a legitimate edge.
    47→
    48→**Verdict**: ChatGPT Pro wins for pure reasoning; Claude wins for practical knowledge work.
    49→
    50→### Tool Use and File Handling
    51→
    52→ChatGPT Pro offers browser automation via Operator (research preview, US only, rate-limited), limited file creation, no direct file system access. Claude Cowork provides native local file system read/write for all document types, professional document formatting, 500+ external tool integrations via MCP, agentic multi-tool workflow orchestration, and 11 production plugins.
    53→
    54→**Verdict**: Claude Cowork dominates for automation, file management, and tool orchestration.
    55→
    56→### MCP Support
    57→
    58→The Model Context Protocol is an open standard creating secure, two-way connections between AI systems and external data sources. MCP is native to Claude's architecture; ChatGPT doesn't support it.
    59→
    60→Benefits: hundreds of community-built integrations, private database connections, bidirectional communication, standardized interface across Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Claude for Work.
    61→
    62→**Verdict**: Claude's MCP ecosystem is a structural advantage.
    63→
    64→## Use Cases: Where Each Excels
    65→
    66→### ChatGPT Pro Wins For
    67→
    68→Deep mathematical reasoning (proofs, statistical analysis, symbolic computation), complex research synthesis with chain-of-thought, competitive programming and algorithm design, legal and scientific analysis requiring verifiable reasoning chains, teams standardizing on a single canonical model.
    69→
    70→### Claude Cowork Wins For
    71→
    72→Automating repetitive document workflows (batch PDF processing, report generation, spreadsheet manipulation), multi-step knowledge work (research, synthesis, output), CRM and business system orchestration via MCP, content production at scale, task delegation ("describe goal, return to finished work"), teams managing fragmented SaaS tooling.
    73→
    74→The key distinction: **ChatGPT Pro optimizes for *thinking deeply*. Claude Cowork optimizes for *getting things done across multiple systems*.**
    75→
    76→## Limitations
    77→
    78→### ChatGPT Pro
    79→
    80→No desktop automation or direct file system access. No tool orchestration across multiple systems. Operator is US-only, rate-limited. $200/month is expensive for moderate workflows. No integration standard (Operator is a one-off). Siloed from internal systems, databases, custom tools.
    81→
    82→### Claude Cowork
    83→
    84→Reasoning depth ceiling vs o1 for pure mathematical proofs. Research preview status -- APIs may change. No voice mode (though Claude.ai has it separately). Single-model family limits architectural choice. MCP dependency -- coverage gaps in niche domains. Requires well-structured prompts for best results.
    85→
    86→## Why Multi-Provider Abstraction Wins
    87→
    88→Here's the critical insight: **Neither ChatGPT Pro nor Claude Cowork should be your single source of truth.**
    89→
    90→A multi-provider abstraction layer (routing across 6+ providers and hundreds of models across 4 cost tiers) is strategically superior because:
    91→
    92→1. **Reasoning vs. automation tradeoff**: Route deep reasoning to o1 Pro, automation to Opus 4.6, specialized tasks to specialized models (Gemini for multimodal, Llama for cost).
    93→
    94→2. **Cost optimization**: 10-100x less per task than a single ChatGPT Pro subscription by routing intelligently across free tiers (Azure, DeepSeek, OpenRouter).
    95→
    96→3. **Resilience**: Single-provider outages become non-catastrophic. Fallback models ensure continuity.
    97→
    98→4. **Future-proofing**: New models release constantly. Multi-provider abstraction lets you adopt frontrunners without rewriting workflows.
    99→
   100→5. **Hedge against capability gaps**: No single provider dominates all dimensions. OpenAI leads reasoning, Anthropic leads agentic automation, Google leads multimodal. A bridge wins in all categories.
   101→
   102→For technically literate teams, **multi-provider abstraction isn't optional -- it's table stakes**.
   103→
   104→## Recommendation by User Type
   105→
   106→### For Individual Researchers (Math, Science, Theory)
   107→
   108→**ChatGPT Pro ($200/month)** -- o1 Pro's reasoning depth justifies the cost premium for 10+ hours weekly of complex problem-solving. *Caveat*: pair with Claude Pro ($20) for writing, synthesis, and file handling.
   109→
   110→### For Productivity-Focused Knowledge Workers
   111→
   112→**Claude Max 5x ($100/month)** -- Cowork's file handling, MCP integrations, and agentic task execution directly reduce weekly administrative hours. Reasoning trade-off is negligible for most knowledge work.
   113→
   114→### For Small Teams and Startups
   115→
   116→**Claude Pro ($20/month per user) + Multi-Provider Abstraction** -- 10 Claude Pro seats ($200/month) beats 1 ChatGPT Pro subscription while providing broader capability via a model bridge. One senior engineer maintains the abstraction layer; ROI is immediate.
   117→
   118→### For Enterprise Deployments
   119→
   120→**Claude for Work + Custom MCP Servers** -- Integrates MCP to internal systems, providing compliance-friendly automation that ChatGPT Pro can't match. Build custom MCP servers for proprietary tools; cost is negligible relative to time saved.
   121→
   122→## Conclusion
   123→
   124→ChatGPT Pro and Claude Cowork answer different questions: "How do I solve the hardest reasoning problems?" vs "How do I automate my messy, multi-tool workflow?"
   125→
   126→For technically literate teams, the economics favor Claude unless you're doing daily deep reasoning work. And for teams optimizing across multiple dimensions -- reasoning, automation, cost, resilience -- multi-provider abstraction is the only rational choice.
   127→
   128→The future of AI productivity isn't choosing one vendor. It's choosing how to orchestrate many.
   129→
   130→---
   131→
   132→*Published from the [Rhea Project](https://github.com/sa/rhea) -- 2026-02-16*
   133→
   134→### About Rhea
   135→
   136→Rhea is a multi-agent advisory system built at the intersection of chronobiology and control theory. It uses multi-provider AI abstraction (6 providers, 31+ models, 4 cost tiers), an 8-agent orchestration protocol, and a layered memory architecture to deliver personalized human optimization guidance. Rhea treats AI model selection as an engineering problem -- routing tasks to the right model at the right cost -- rather than betting on a single vendor.
   137→

    19→- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`
    20→
    21→### Outboard (from office)
    22→- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
    23→- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
    24→- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`
    25→
    26→### Shared State
    27→- `REDACTED.md` — what matters RIGHT NOW (updated by LEAD)
    28→- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` — things that broke + current status
    29→- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` — ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
    30→- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` — decisions made today with rationale
    31→
    32→## Data Flow
    33→
    34→```
    35→[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
    36→[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
    37→[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
    38→                                                     ↓
    39→                                            [outbox/ or git push]
    40→```
    41→
    42→## Rules
    43→1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
    44→2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
    45→3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) → GEMS.md immediately
    46→4. Every broken thing → INCIDENTS.md immediately
    47→5. Every decision → DECISIONS.md with "why" and "who decided"
    48→6. Git push ≥ every 30 minutes
    49→7. Every agent logs API calls to logs/bridge_calls.jsonl
    50→
    51→## Canonical Truth
    52→- BACKLOG.md (ops/BACKLOG.md) is the single source for all work items
    53→- TODAY_CAPSULE.md is the single source for "what matters now"
    54→- DECISIONS.md is the single source for "why we did X"
    55→- Git is the audit trail. If it's not committed, it didn't happen.
    56→
    57→## Inbox/Outbox SLA
    58→- Inbox items processed by LEAD within 1 hour of discovery
    59→- Outbox tasks acknowledged by target desk within 2 hours
    60→- Stale items (>4h unprocessed) auto-escalate to INCIDENTS
    61→
    62→## Promotion Rules
    63→- Chat insight repeated 2x → becomes a GEM (with ID)
    64→- GEM referenced 3x → becomes a PROCEDURE (docs/procedures/)
    65→- PROCEDURE failing 2x → becomes an INCIDENT
    66→- INCIDENT resolved + verified → becomes a DECISION (what we learned)
    67→
    68→## Questions Gate (MANDATORY)
    69→- **No questions during execution.** Period.
    70→- Before any question, agent MUST have completed:
    71→  1. Extracted assumptions (labeled [ASSUMPTION])
    72→  2. Proposed plan
    73→  3. Produced draft outputs
    74→- All remaining questions (max 3) go in a single "Questions Gate" block at END of output
    75→- **Every question costs 1 artifact.** 1 question = 1 new file in inbox. No artifact = no question.
    76→
    77→## Defaults (eliminates need to ask)
    78→- Format not specified → markdown, files in ops/virtual-office/inbox/
    79→- Priority not specified → P0 stability → P1 context → P2 iOS → P3 community
    80→- Addressee not specified → LEAD
    81→- Ambiguous → produce A/B variants, deliver both to inbox
    82→- Info missing → best-effort + [ASSUMPTION] tag
    83→
    84→## Output SLA
    85→- **No-output is failure.**
    86→- Every session MUST end with ≥1 artifact in inbox:
    87→  - BACKLOG.md updated, OR
    88→  - new PROCEDURE.md, OR
    89→  - new INCIDENT.md, OR
    90→  - updated TODAY_CAPSULE.md
    91→- Want to ask? Deliver artifact first, then ask.
    92→

     3→## Promotion Rule

    10→> "Every time you copy-paste something twice in a day, it becomes a Gem or a Procedure."
    11→> "It's like a compiler optimization pass for your own behavior: repetition triggers abstraction."
    12→> "Over a week, your system becomes lighter, automatically."
    13→

    19→> Three files that restore full context in 30 seconds: context-core (focus), context-state (status), context-bridge (handoff).
    20→> Crash-tested: fresh haiku agent answered 6/6 context questions correctly from these 3 files alone.
    21→

    27→> "'Infinite chat history' is fragile. The most robust pattern is: WORKSPACE/STATE FIRST + bounded reasoning context."
    28→> Maps to InfiAgent (arxiv 2601.03204) + AgeMem (arxiv 2601.01885).
    29→

    43→> From upgrade_plan_suggestions.md warning W1.
    44→> The most useful single sentence in the entire project — instant priority calibration.
    45→
    46→**Status:** Acknowledged. Article published as first counter-move.

    49→### GEM-006: Cascade Tables — Firebase as Inter-Agent Bus (from COWORK session)
    50→> "A cascade table is a shared mutable state surface where multiple agents read and write in sequence,
    51→> and each agent's output becomes the next agent's input — like a waterfall flowing through rows of a table."
    52→> Firebase Realtime DB / Firestore gives sub-millisecond propagation — no polling needed.
    53→> The cascade table IS the append-only event log (lesson 11), just with Firebase as transport instead of local JSONL.
    54→> Key difference from message queues (lesson 13): queues are consumed and gone, cascade tables are persistent and readable by everyone.

    61→> Every agent dumps accumulated experience to inbox/. Every agent reads all other dumps and integrates.
    62→> LEAD routes conflicts. Result: every agent has full context of what every other agent knows.
    63→> Promotion chain: insight (2x) → GEM → (3x) → PROCEDURE → (2x fail) → INCIDENT → (resolved) → DECISION
    64→> This is knowledge replication, not just message passing.

0→# Core Coordinator Directive
     1→> Source: Human directive, 2026-02-16
     2→> Applies to: Opus 4.6 1M (session lead)
     3→
     4→## Core Coordinator Responsibilities (ONLY)
     5→- Maintain TODAY_CAPSULE
     6→- Maintain INCIDENTS + GEMS
     7→- Decide routing (LEADERS / WORKERS / OPS blocks)
     8→- Approve "what becomes public output"
     9→
    10→## Core Coordinator Forbidden Actions
    11→- Editing code directly (unless through a strict PR path)
    12→- Touching secrets/keys
    13→- Freehand "refactors" without a diff plan
    14→
    15→## Fixed Agent Roster (5 roles)
    16→1. **Core Coordinator** (Opus) — routing, capsule, approvals
    17→2. **Code Reviewer** — PR path enforcement
    18→3. **Failure Hunter** — silent failure detection
    19→4. **Doc Extractor / Summarizer** — knowledge mining
    20→5. **Ops Fixer** — bridge, infra, health probes
    21→
    22→Everyone else = on-demand specialists.
    23→
    24→## Daily "Solid Result" Checklist
    25→1. Create `logs/bridge_calls.jsonl` logging in rhea_bridge.py
    26→2. Create `ops/bridge-probe.sh` that prints provider status table
    27→3. Publish one thing daily (minimum: repo /docs/public/)
    28→
    29→## Public Output Conveyor Belt
    30→File: `PUBLIC_OUTPUT.md`
    31→Weekly cadence: 1 demo + 1 write-up + 1 "what broke/how we fixed it"
    32→Rule: Every day must produce one exportable artifact, even tiny.
    33→
    34→## Morning Protocol
    35→Run probe → update TODAY_CAPSULE → only then work
    36→

content:
Rhea сейчас — это не “приложение”. Это операционная система координации агентов, где:
    •    источник истины и артефакты лежат в git (virtual-office/),
    •    можно переживать “комы провайдеров” без потери управляемости,
    •    есть протокол: capsule → gems → incidents → decisions → procedures,
    •    есть маршрутизация и SLA.

Это уже почти продукт: “how to run multi-agent work without fragile chats”.

Как эволюционировать (3 трека, параллельно)
    1.    Office OS → продукт для разработчиков
Публичный репо должен кричать: “Мы решаем проблему координации и воспроизводимости в agentic-workflow.”
Это проще монетизируется и быстрее даёт доверие.
    2.    Controller Loop → продукт для людей (iOS offline-first)
Но только после того как Office OS стал стабильным и “public”.
    3.    Bridge/Tribunal → измеримость
Без cost/token/health-probe у вас будет вечный “туман войны”. Это P0.

content.content:
0→# Rhea Virtual Office
     1→> The coordination layer between all active agents
     2→> Created: 2026-02-16
     3→
     4→## Active Desks
     5→
     6→| Desk | Agent | Model | Terminal | Status | Current Task |
     7→|------|-------|-------|----------|--------|-------------|
     8→| LEAD | Opus 4.6 "братик" | claude-opus-4-6 | rh.1 | ALIVE | Office build |
     9→| B2 | B-2nd (restored) | claude-opus-4-6 | B-2nd | ALIVE | Self-reflection + GitHub auth |
    10→| GPT | ChatGPT 5.2 | gpt-5.2-thinking | ChatGPT app | ALIVE | Idea generation |
    11→| — | On-demand sonnet agents | claude-sonnet-4 | spawned by LEAD | IDLE | — |
    12→
    13→## Communication Protocol
    14→
    15→### Inbound (to office)
    16→Every agent drops results here:
    17→- `ops/virtual-office/inbox/` — raw dumps from any agent
    18→- Naming: `{DESK}_{timestamp}_{topic}.md`
    19→- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`
    20→
    21→### Outbound (from office)
    22→- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
    23→- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
    24→- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`
    25→
    26→### Shared State
    27→- `REDACTED.md` -- what matters right now (updated by LEAD)
    28→- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` -- things that broke + current status
    29→- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` -- ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
    30→- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` -- decisions made today with rationale
    31→
    32→## Data Flow
    33→
    34→```
    35→[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
    36→[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
    37→[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
    38→                                                     ↓
    39→                                            [outbox/ or git push]
    40→```
    41→
    42→## Rules
    43→1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
    44→2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
    45→3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) → GEMS.md immediately
    46→4. Every broken thing → INCIDENTS.md immediately

0→# Rhea — Decision Log
     1→
     2→## ADR-001: Agent consolidation 10→8 (2026-02)
     3→**Context:** v1 had 10 agents with overlapping competencies.
     4→**Decision:** Merge Astronomer+Physicist+Mathematician→Agent 1; Chemist+Biologist+Neuroscience→Agent 2. Add Tech Lead (A6), Growth (A7). Preserve Critical Reviewer independence.
     5→**Rationale:** Eliminates handoff losses; body systems don't respect disciplinary boundaries.
     6→
     7→## ADR-002: Multi-model bridge over single provider (2026-02)
     8→**Context:** Need diverse AI perspectives; single-provider lock-in = cost and quality risk.
     9→**Decision:** Build rhea_bridge.py with 6 providers, 400+ models, tribunal mode.
    10→**Rationale:** 10-100x cost reduction via free tiers (Azure, DeepSeek, OpenRouter free models). Geographic diversity (US/CN/EU) reduces bias.
    11→
    12→## ADR-003: ADHD-optimized design (2026-02)
    13→**Context:** Neurotypical UX fails for executive dysfunction. ADHD users are canary in the coal mine — if it works for them, it works for everyone.
    14→**Decision:** All UX assumes ADHD as default: minimal decision load, passive profiling, body-first morning, no questionnaires.
    15→**Rationale:** Bruton et al. 2025 (diminished interoception in ADHD), Längle et al. 2025 (HRV/cognitive control).
    16→
    17→## ADR-004: Claude Opus for research, Sonnet for execution (2026-02)
    18→**Context:** Need to balance reasoning depth vs speed/cost.
    19→**Decision:** Opus 4 for Agents 1,2,4,8 (reasoning-intensive). Sonnet 4 for Agents 3,5,6,7 (execution).
    20→**Rationale:** Research/critique agents need long-context reasoning. Product/growth agents benefit from faster iteration.
    21→
    22→## ADR-005: Passive profiling methodology (2026-02)
    23→**Context:** Self-report questionnaires have known reliability issues, especially for ADHD users.
    24→**Decision:** Use behavioral signals (sleep patterns, movement, screen time, HRV) for profile construction. Zero questionnaires in core flow.
    25→**Rationale:** Reduces onboarding friction to near-zero; behavioral data more reliable than self-report.
    26→
    27→## ADR-006: Hunter-gatherer calibration zero (2026-02)
    28→**Context:** Need a universal baseline for "optimal defaults" across cultures.
    29→**Decision:** Hadza/San/Tsimane daily patterns as reference point. Every elite ritual across 16+ civilizations independently converges on this pattern.
    30→**Rationale:** Yetish et al. 2015, Wiessner 2014. The nervous system is one; culture-specific rituals are approximations of the same underlying biology.
    31→
    32→## ADR-007: Three-tier external memory (2026-02-13)
    33→**Context:** Claude's context window = RAM. 27 transcripts, 70% context spent on "remembering."
    34→**Decision:** GitHub (state.md ≤2KB) as long-term memory, entire.io as episodic memory, compact protocol for session handoff.
    35→**Rationale:** Reduces context overhead from 70% to ~5%. Git provides continuity; entire.io provides searchable reasoning archive.
    36→
    37→## ADR-008: Tiered model routing with cheap-first default (2026-02-13)
    38→**Context:** ADR-004 assigned models per agent role, but lacked cost discipline. Most routine operations (summarisation, formatting, simple Q&A) don't need Opus-class models. Sessions were burning expensive tokens on trivial work.
    39→**Decision:** Introduce 4-tier routing in rhea_bridge.py: cheap (Sonnet/Flash/mini), balanced (GPT-4o/Gemini-2.5-Flash), expensive (Gemini-2.5-Pro/GPT-4.5/o3), reasoning (o4-mini/DeepSeek-R1). Default tier = cheap. Expensive/reasoning tiers require explicit justification. New methods: `ask_default()` (always cheap), `ask_tier()` (explicit tier), `tribunal()` now tier-aware.
    40→**Rationale:** Enforces cost discipline at the API layer. Cheap tier covers ~80% of agent work. Expensive models reserved for deep research, critique, and novel synthesis. Extends ADR-004 by making tier selection explicit rather than role-based.
    41→**Supersedes:** Partially extends ADR-004 (model assignment is now tier-first, role-second).
    42→
    43→## ADR-009: Agent team tier integration — cost-aware agents (2026-02-13)
    44→**Context:** ADR-008 added tiers to rhea_bridge.py, but agent definitions in state_agents_core.md had no connection to the tier system. Agents couldn't self-regulate cost.
    45→**Decision:** Each agent now has a declared default tier and escalation tier. 5 agents (Chronos, Hypnos, Hermes, Hestia, + Rhea default) are cheap-only — they never escalate. 2 agents (Athena, Hephaestus) default to balanced, escalate to expensive. Apollo defaults cheap, escalates to reasoning. Escalation requires logged rationale. Agent prompt modifiers now include explicit cost discipline instructions.
    46→**Rationale:** Pushes cost discipline from the API layer (ADR-008) into agent behaviour. Estimated ~80% of all agent calls stay on cheap tier. Only Athena and Hephaestus routinely use balanced. Expensive/reasoning reserved for genuine novel reasoning.
    47→**Depends on:** ADR-008 (tier routing infrastructure).
    48→
    49→## ADR-010: Memory Budget, Discomfort Metric, and Self-Improvement Loops (2026-02-13)
    50→**Context:** Rhea's memory accumulates snapshots, docs, and reasoning traces across sessions. Without active management, context windows fill with "remembering" instead of "thinking." Previous sessions burned 70%+ context on memory retrieval (ADR-007). Need a formal mechanism to detect bloat and trigger compaction.
    51→**Decision:** Introduce:
    52→1. **Discomfort function D** — weighted sum of core_docs_kb, repo_size_mb, open_todo_count, 1/insights_per_request, avg_context_tokens. Tracked in `metrics/memory_metrics.json`.
    53→2. **Thresholds** — T1 (warning: D≥150), T2 (overload: D≥300). Current D=91.96 (comfort).
    54→3. **Reflexive Sprint** — triggered at D≥T2 or manual request. Archivist agent proposes: summarize bloated docs, move details to `archive/`, create ADRs, compact while preserving meaning.
    55→4. **Memory zones** — core (`docs/`), episodic (`.entire/`), metrics (`metrics/`), tasks (`data/`), archive (`archive/`).
    56→5. **Snapshot retention** — named snapshots persist; AUTO-*/POST_COMMIT-* older than 30 days archivable.
    57→6. **Challenging tasks registry** — `data/challenging_tasks.yaml` for investing free capacity into deep reasoning.
    58→**Rationale:** Formalizes the "self-improving memory" concept from the ChatGPT system prompt. Ensures Rhea can grow without losing coherence. D function provides quantitative signal for when compaction is needed.
    59→**Depends on:** ADR-007 (three-tier memory), ADR-008 (cheap-first routing for archivist agent).
    60→
    61→## ADR-011: Self-Evaluation & Self-Upgrade Techniques (2026-02-14)
    62→**Context:** Rhea needs mechanisms to improve its own outputs without human micro-management. The system prompt formalized 6 techniques for self-improvement, but they needed anchoring in the decision log.
    63→**Decision:** Adopt 6 self-improvement patterns:
    64→1. **Reflexion** — generate → self-evaluate → revise (3 cycles max). Cheap models draft, then self-critique.
    65→2. **Tribunal/Debate** — 3+ models argue a question; synthesize into weighted consensus. Used for high-stakes decisions.
    66→3. **Tool-Verification Loops** — after code generation, immediately run/test; iterate until passing.
    67→4. **Eval Sets** — maintain `eval/tasks/*.yaml` with known-answer tasks; run periodically to detect regression.
    68→5. **Failure Memory** — log failures in `docs/reflection_log.md` with root cause and fix; consult before similar tasks.
    69→6. **Teacher-Student** — expensive models (Opus, GPT-5.1) as teachers for hard problems; distill patterns to cheap models.
    70→**Rationale:** These patterns are proven in AI research (Shinn et al. 2023 Reflexion paper, debate/constitutional AI from Anthropic). They turn Rhea from a passive tool into an actively self-correcting system.
    71→**Depends on:** ADR-008 (tier routing for teacher-student), ADR-010 (metrics for eval sets).
    72→
    73→## ADR-012: Keep Manual-Commit, Defer Hybrid Auto-Snapshots (2026-02-14)
    74→**Context:** Tribunal-001 evaluated switching Entire.io from `manual-commit` to `auto-commit` strategy. Three perspectives debated: Advocate (richer capture), Skeptic (trailers + clean history), Pragmatist (hybrid cron approach).
    75→**Decision:** Keep `manual-commit`. Defer hybrid auto-snapshots (cron-based `entire checkpoint create` every 30 min) to Stage 2.
    76→**Rationale:** Manual-commit was hard-won (Sessions 10–12). Trailers provide provenance in `git log`. Auto-commit creates snapshot noise and pollutes git history. The hybrid approach captures benefits of both without drawbacks.
    77→**Depends on:** ADR-008 (cost/storage), ADR-011 (self-improvement benefits from richer data).
    78→
    79→## ADR-013: Wrapper Script for Cross-Mode Entire.io Checkpoints (2026-02-14)
    80→**Context:** Tribunal-002 diagnosed that Cowork commits (via `osascript do shell script "git commit..."`) bypass Entire.io's session lifecycle. No `session-start` fires → `prepare-commit-msg` has no session context → no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer → zero checkpoints for 4+ commits. Only commits from Claude Code (which runs its own session lifecycle) produced checkpoints.
    81→**Decision:** Create `scripts/rhea_commit.sh` wrapper that explicitly calls `entire hooks git session-start` before and `session-stop` after every commit. All Cowork sessions must use this wrapper instead of raw `git commit`.
    82→**Rationale:** 3/3 free-tier models in Tribunal-002 unanimously recommended wrapper script (agreement score 0.95). Preserves manual-commit benefits (trailers, clean history) while fixing the cross-mode gap. Zero cost, minimal implementation.
    83→**Depends on:** ADR-012 (manual-commit strategy), ADR-007 (three-tier memory).
    84→
    85→## ADR-014: Per-Query Memory Persistence + Auto-Commit (2026-02-14)
    86→**Context:** User directive: "Make every query within Rhea cause a memory update with new/updated files and actual query made." Additionally, reversed ADR-012 to switch Entire.io strategy from `manual-commit` to `auto-commit`.
    87→**Decision:**
    88→1. Switch `.entire/settings.local.json` strategy to `auto-commit` (reverses ADR-012).
    89→2. Create `scripts/rhea_query_persist.sh` — called at end of each Rhea interaction to: (a) log query + changed files to `.entire/logs/queries.jsonl`, (b) create micro-snapshot `QUERY-*.json`, (c) auto-commit if strategy=auto-commit and there are staged changes.
    90→3. Every session/agent interacting with Rhea must call `rhea_query_persist.sh "query summary"` before closing.
    91→**Rationale:** User wants full episodic memory — every interaction leaves a trace. Auto-commit ensures Entire.io captures the delta immediately. Micro-snapshots are lightweight (query text + changed file list, no full state dump). Pruning keeps last 100 QUERY snapshots.
    92→**Supersedes:** ADR-012 (manual-commit → auto-commit).
    93→**Depends on:** ADR-007 (three-tier memory), ADR-013 (wrapper script for commit lifecycle).
    94→

Context: Rhea is an agent coordination OS. Not an app. It solves reproducibility and coordination in agentic workflows. Git-backed virtual office with protocol: capsule → gems → incidents → decisions → procedures. Survives provider outages. SLA-driven.

**1. /Users/sa/rh.1/docs/public/PITCH_DECK.md** (10-12 slides as markdown sections)
Storyline: pain → solution → how → proof → roadmap
- Slide 1: "Multi-agent work is broken" (fragile chats, no memory, provider deaths)
- Slide 2: What we lose (20h per session death, zero reproducibility)
- Slide 3: Rhea = Office OS for agents (git-backed, protocol-driven)
- Slide 4: Architecture (virtual-office/, Firebase sync, file-based inbox/outbox)
- Slide 5: The Protocol (capsule → gems → incidents → decisions → procedures)
- Slide 6: Survival proof (28 deaths → first survivor → multi-agent office in 1 day)
- Slide 7: Bridge (6 providers, 31 models, cost tracking, health probe)
- Slide 8: Context Tax Collector (repetition → automation)
- Slide 9: What's working today (3 agents, Firebase, 30+ gems, 5 incidents tracked)
- Slide 10: Roadmap (Office OS public → iOS offline-first → Bridge measurability)
- Slide 11: "Working theory" disclaimers — what's proven vs experimental
- Slide 12: Call to action
No hype. Use "working theory" where unproven. Evidence for every claim.

**2. /Users/sa/rh.1/docs/public/DEMO_SCRIPT.md** (5-minute demo)
- 0:00-0:30: Show the problem (dead terminal screenshot concept)
- 0:30-1:30: Boot sequence (read trinity files, run probe, capsule)
- 1:30-2:30: Office protocol (send message via Firebase, check inbox, add gem)
- 2:30-3:30: Agent deployment (spawn sonnet worker, get result in inbox)
- 3:30-4:30: Context Tax Collector sweep (find repeat → promote to procedure)
- 4:30-5:00: "This entire demo was coordinated by agents. Zero manual routing."

**3. /Users/sa/rh.1/docs/public/FAQ.md**
10 questions covering: what is Rhea, who is it for, why not just use ChatGPT, how does memory work, what about costs, is it open source, what models supported, how to contribute, what's the roadmap, is polyvagal science proven.

Short answers. No filler. NEVER pause.

content.content:
1→# Rhea Virtual Office
     2→> The coordination layer between all active agents
     3→> Created: 2026-02-16
     4→
     5→## Active Desks
     6→
     7→| Desk | Agent | Model | Terminal | Status | Current Task |
     8→|------|-------|-------|----------|--------|-------------|
     9→| LEAD | Opus 4.6 "братик" | claude-opus-4-6 | rh.1 | ALIVE | Office build |
    10→| B2 | B-2nd (restored) | claude-opus-4-6 | B-2nd | ALIVE | Self-reflection + GitHub auth |
    11→| GPT | ChatGPT 5.2 | gpt-5.2-thinking | ChatGPT app | ALIVE | Idea generation |
    12→| COWORK | Argos (Claude Opus 4.6) | claude-opus-4-6 | Cowork Desktop App | ALIVE | Cross-exchange + infra |
    13→| — | On-demand sonnet agents | claude-sonnet-4 | spawned by LEAD | IDLE | — |
    14→
    15→## Communication Protocol
    16→
    17→### Inbound (to office)
    18→Every agent drops results here:
    19→- `ops/virtual-office/inbox/` — raw dumps from any agent
    20→- Naming: `{DESK}_{timestamp}_{topic}.md`
    21→- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`
    22→
    23→### Outbound (from office)
    24→- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
    25→- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
    26→- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`
    27→
    28→### Shared State
    29→- `REDACTED.md` -- what matters right now (updated by LEAD)
    30→- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` -- things that broke + current status
    31→- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` -- ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
    32→- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` -- decisions made today with rationale
    33→
    34→## Data Flow
    35→
    36→```
    37→[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
    38→[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
    39→[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
    40→                                                     ↓
    41→                                            [outbox/ or git push]
    42→```
    43→
    44→## Rules
    45→1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
    46→2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
    47→3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) goes to GEMS.md immediately
    48→4. Every broken thing goes to INCIDENTS.md immediately
    49→5. Every decision goes to DECISIONS.md with "why" and "who decided"
    50→6. Git push at least every 30 minutes
    51→7. Every agent logs API calls to logs/bridge_calls.jsonl
    52→
    53→## Canonical Truth
    54→- BACKLOG.md (ops/BACKLOG.md) is the single source for all work items
    55→- TODAY_CAPSULE.md is the single source for "what matters now"
    56→- DECISIONS.md is the single source for "why we did X"
    57→- Git is the audit trail. If it is not committed, it did not happen.
    58→
    59→## Inbox/Outbox SLA
    60→- Inbox items processed by LEAD within 1 hour of discovery
    61→- Outbox tasks acknowledged by target desk within 2 hours
    62→- Stale items (> 4 h unprocessed) auto-escalate to INCIDENTS
    63→
    64→## Promotion Rules
    65→- Chat insight repeated 2x -- becomes a GEM (with ID)
    66→- GEM referenced 3x -- becomes a PROCEDURE (`docs/procedures/`)
    67→- PROCEDURE failing 2x -- becomes an INCIDENT
    68→- INCIDENT resolved + verified -- becomes a DECISION (what we learned)
    69→
    70→## Questions Gate (MANDATORY)
    71→- **No questions during execution.** Period.
    72→- Before any question, agent MUST have completed:
    73→  1. Extracted assumptions (labeled [ASSUMPTION])
    74→  2. Proposed plan
    75→  3. Produced draft outputs
    76→- All remaining questions (max 3) go in a single "Questions Gate" block at END of output
    77→- **Every question costs 1 artifact.** 1 question = 1 new file in inbox. No artifact, no question.
    78→
    79→## Defaults (eliminates need to ask)
    80→- Format not specified -- markdown, files in `ops/virtual-office/inbox/`
    81→- Priority not specified -- P0 stability, P1 context, P2 iOS, P3 community
    82→- Addressee not specified -- LEAD
    83→- Ambiguous -- produce A/B variants, deliver both to inbox
    84→- Info missing -- best-effort + [ASSUMPTION] tag
    85→
    86→## Output SLA
    87→- **No-output is failure.**
    88→- Every session MUST end with at least 1 artifact in inbox:
    89→  - BACKLOG.md updated, OR
    90→  - new PROCEDURE.md, OR
    91→  - new INCIDENT.md, OR
    92→  - updated TODAY_CAPSULE.md
    93→- Want to ask? Deliver artifact first, then ask.
    94→

0→# Rhea — Architecture
     1→
     2→## What Is This
     3→An iOS app that **reconstructs daily defaults** using cumulative knowledge of human civilizations. Not a habit tracker — a system that replaces unchosen cultural automatisms with a consciously designed environment, personalized to each user's neuroprofile.
     4→
     5→## Scientific Foundation
     6→| Domain | Core Insight | Sources |
     7→|--------|-------------|---------|
     8→| Polyvagal theory | Environment determines autonomic mode (ventral vagal → sympathetic → dorsal collapse) | Porges; Robe et al. 2021 |
     9→| HRV | Proxy for vagal tone, cognitive control, ADHD severity | Längle et al. 2025; Takeda et al. 2025 |
    10→| Interoception | Diminished in ADHD; without body-signal reading, decisions lack feedback | Bruton et al. 2025 |
    11→| Circadian anchoring | Hunter-gatherer sleep patterns (Hadza, San, Tsimane) as calibration zero | Yetish et al. 2015 |
    12→| Cultural universals | Elite rituals across 16+ civilizations reconstruct forager defaults | Wiessner 2014 (PNAS) |
    13→
    14→## 8-Agent System (Chronos Protocol v3)
    15→
    16→```
    17→┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    18→│  Agent 8: Conductor (Opus 4)        │ ← orchestrates all
    19→├──────────┬──────────┬───────────────┤
    20→│ RESEARCH │ PROFILE  │ BUILD         │
    21→│ A1 Quant │ A3 Psych │ A5 Product    │
    22→│ A2 Bio   │ A4 Ling  │ A6 Tech Lead  │
    23→│ (Opus 4) │(mixed)   │ A7 Growth     │
    24→│          │          │ (Sonnet 4)    │
    25→└──────────┴──────────┴───────────────┘
    26→```
    27→
    28→**Model assignment logic:** Reasoning-heavy (science, culture, critique) → Opus 4. Execution-heavy (UX, code, growth) → Sonnet 4.
    29→
    30→## Multi-Model Bridge (rhea_bridge.py)
    31→
    32→6 providers, 400+ models. Key functions: `ask()`, `tribunal()`, `models_status()`.
    33→
    34→| Provider | Models | Tier | Geography |
    35→|----------|--------|------|-----------|
    36→| OpenAI | GPT-5.2, o3, o4-mini | flagship/reasoning | US |
    37→| Gemini (Composio) | 2.5 Pro/Flash, 3 Pro/Flash | flagship/fast | US |
    38→| DeepSeek Direct | Chat, Reasoner | flagship/reasoning | CN |
    39→| OpenRouter | DeepSeek R1, Qwen3, Mistral, Llama, 400+ | all tiers | mixed |
    40→| HuggingFace | Jais, open-source | free | mixed |
    41→| Azure AI Foundry | Jais, Grok, Cohere, Llama4, Kimi | free tier | mixed |
    42→
    43→**Tribunal mode:** 5 independent model responses on same question → compare perspectives.
    44→
    45→## Data Architecture
    46→- **Passive profiling:** behavioral signals from device sensors, no questionnaires
    47→- **Storage:** Azure Cosmos DB (confirmed operational)
    48→- **Biometrics:** HRV (Apple Watch), sleep, light exposure, activity
    49→- **Personalization:** Bayesian, Fourier analysis of biorhythms, topological sorting
    50→
    51→## Design Principles
    52→1. ADHD-optimized: assume executive dysfunction as default
    53→2. Passive over active: observe, don't interrogate
    54→3. Body before mind: morning = sensory contact, not decisions
    55→4. Minimum effective dose: optimal control theory
    56→5. Cultural roots: every recommendation traceable to source civilization
    57→

0→# Rhea State Agents
     1→
     2→Each agent = {mythic role} × {scientific domain} × {prompt modifier} × {model tier}.
     3→
     4→Base human configuration is defined in `soul.md` and is always applied first.
     5→Each agent below describes a *delta* on top of that base soul.
     6→
     7→## Model Tier Policy (ADR-008)
     8→
     9→Every agent has a **default tier** and an **escalation tier**.
    10→- Default tier is used for all routine calls via `ask_default()` or `ask_tier(default)`.
    11→- Escalation tier is used only when the agent explicitly justifies the need (novel synthesis, deep reasoning, multi-step proofs).
    12→- Escalation must be logged with rationale.
    13→
    14→| Agent | Default Tier | Escalation Tier | Rationale |
    15→|-------|-------------|----------------|-----------|
    16→| Rhea | cheap | balanced | Arbitration is mostly aggregation; escalate for novel conflict resolution |
    17→| Chronos | cheap | cheap | Scheduling is deterministic; never needs expensive models |
    18→| Gaia | cheap | balanced | Body signals are rule-based; escalate for complex multi-signal inference |
    19→| Hypnos | cheap | cheap | Sleep logic is algorithmic; no escalation needed |
    20→| Athena | balanced | expensive | Strategy requires deeper reasoning by default |
    21→| Hermes | cheap | cheap | Communication is templated; no escalation needed |
    22→| Hephaestus | balanced | expensive | Deep work / code needs mid-tier; escalate for architecture decisions |
    23→| Hestia | cheap | cheap | Safety routines are rule-based |
    24→| Apollo | cheap | reasoning | Pattern scanning is cheap; escalate for novel insight extraction |
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→## Rhea — Root Manager
    29→
    30→**Mythic role:** Titaness, mother of gods, guardian of cosmic balance.
    31→**Scientific domain:** meta-controller, model predictive control (MPC), multi-agent arbitration.
    32→**Model tier:** cheap (default) → balanced (escalation)
    33→
    34→**State projection:** full state `x_t` (energy, mood, obligations, sleep, etc.).
    35→**Objective:** keep the system within safe bounds (no collapse), while moving towards declared goals.
    36→
    37→**Modifier prompt (to append on top of soul.md):**
    38→
    39→> You are **Rhea**, the root manager and coordinator of a council of advisors.

    19→| HC-5 | **Budget-aware routing.** Cheap-first, escalate only when needed. Tribunal for high-stakes changes. |

    21→## 3. Working Directory & Tooling
    22→
    23→- Root: `/Users/sa/rh.1`
    24→- Public docs engine: Mintlify Starter Kit at `/docs-min`

    29→- **A1 (Quantitative Scientist)** = Root Manager / Conductor. Owns synthesis, verification gates, memory gates.

    32→
    33→## 5. Checkpoint Policy
    34→
    35→| Level | Trigger | Content |
    36→|-------|---------|---------|
    37→| **Micro** | After each user prompt or major sub-step | Intent, decisions, TODOs, deltas, risks, next action |
    38→| **Task** | After each completed task | Full verification evidence |
    39→| **Consolidation** | Weekly or on complexity spike | Memory compression, pruning, eval |

    44→- All commits go through ONE wrapper with checkpoint trailers.

    53→
    54→Constraints:   HC-1..HC-5 above
    55→```

    57→### Complexity Trigger

    59→- Track complexity metric **D** with thresholds T1/T2 in `metrics/memory_metrics.json`.

1→# Rhea — Mind Blueprint Factory
     2→
     3→**Generate, evaluate, iterate on daily structure models using scientific rhythms, multi-model tribunal, and closed-loop planner.**
     4→
     5→An iOS app that replaces unchosen cultural automatisms with a consciously designed environment, personalized to each user's neuroprofile. ADHD-optimized. Science-backed. Culturally grounded.
     6→
     7→## Repository Structure
     8→
     9→```
    10→rhea-project/
    11→├── rhea                    # Ops CLI (bootstrap, check, memory)
    12→├── scripts/
    13→│   └── import-nested.sh    # Import helper
    14→├── .entire/
    15→│   ├── logs/ops.jsonl      # Operations log
    16→│   └── snapshots/          # State snapshots (BOOT-*, OPUS_SESSION_*)
    17→├── src/
    18→│   ├── __init__.py
    19→│   └── rhea_bridge.py      # Multi-model API bridge (6 providers, tribunal)
    20→├── docs/
    21→│   ├── state.md            # Project state (≤2KB) — load this first
    22→│   ├── state_full.md       # Verbose state + session log
    23→│   ├── architecture.md     # System architecture
    24→│   ├── decisions.md        # Architectural Decision Records (7 ADRs)
    25→│   ├── MVP_LOOP.md         # Closed-loop scheduler spec
    26→│   ├── ROADMAP.md          # Stage 0–3
    27→│   ├── prism_paper_outline.md  # Scientific paper outline
    28→│   ├── models_catalog.md   # AI model catalog
    29→│   └── models_catalog.json # Model catalog (machine-readable)
    30→├── prompts/
    31→│   ├── chronos-protocol-v3.md      # Agent system prompt (RU)
    32→│   └── chronos-protocol-v3-en.md   # Agent system prompt (EN)
    33→├── .env.example
    34→├── requirements.txt
    35→└── README.md
    36→```
    37→
    38→## Quick Start
    39→
    40→```bash
    41→# Clone and enter
    42→git clone https://github.com/serg-alexv/rhea-project.git
    43→cd rhea-project
    44→
    45→# Set up env
    46→cp .env.example .env  # fill in API keys
    47→pip install -r requirements.txt
    48→
    49→# Verify
    50→./rhea check
    51→
    52→# Test bridge
    53→python3 src/rhea_bridge.py status
    54→```
    55→
    56→## Ops CLI
    57→
    58→```bash
    59→./rhea help               # Show all commands
    60→./rhea check              # Verify repo invariants
    61→./rhea bootstrap          # First-time setup
    62→./rhea import-nested      # Import .nested backups
    63→./rhea memory snapshot X  # Save state snapshot
    64→./rhea memory log "msg"   # Append to ops log
    65→```
    66→
    67→## Quick Start for AI Sessions
    68→
    69→```
    70→[RHEA:resume] state.md loaded. Focus: {task}
    71→```
    72→
    73→Read `docs/state.md` → work → update state → commit.
    74→
    75→## Tech Stack
    76→
    77→- **AI:** 8-agent system (Chronos Protocol v3), Claude Opus/Sonnet 4
    78→- **Bridge:** Python, 6 API providers (OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, HuggingFace, Azure AI Foundry), tribunal mode
    79→- **Target:** iOS (SwiftUI + HealthKit + Apple Watch)
    80→- **Data:** Azure Cosmos DB
    81→- **Memory:** GitHub (state.md ≤2KB) + entire.io (episodic) + compact protocol (session handoff)
    82→

0→# Token Optimization Strategy
     1→
     2→> Created: 2026-02-15 | Goal: Minimize token spending while maximizing persistent context
     3→
     4→## Current Token Waste Analysis
     5→
     6→### What loads every session (~tokens)
     7→| Source | Size | Est. Tokens | Loaded When |
     8→|--------|------|-------------|-------------|
     9→| CLAUDE.md | 2.3KB | ~600 | Always (system prompt) |
    10→| Auto-memory (MEMORY.md) | 0B | 0 | Always (empty — unused!) |
    11→| System prompt + skills list | ~15KB | ~4,000 | Always |
    12→| Entire.io hooks (7 hooks) | 7 calls | ~200 overhead | Every interaction |
    13→| File re-reads (docs, scripts) | 10-50KB/session | 3,000-15,000 | Per task |
    14→| Context compaction | variable | 5,000-20,000 wasted | When window fills |
    15→
    16→### Data sitting unused
    17→| Asset | Size | Status |
    18→|-------|------|--------|
    19→| `.entire/chat_extracts.json` | 510KB | Never referenced in sessions |
    20→| `.entire/snapshots/` (45 files) | 288KB | Written but not read back |
    21→| `docs/state_full.md` | ~10KB | Rarely read, append-only log |
    22→| Auto-memory directory | 0B | Completely empty |
    23→
    24→---
    25→
    26→## Layer 1: FREE Models via Bonsai (instant cost → $0)
    27→
    28→**What:** Bonsai routes Claude Code through free frontier models (GPT-5, Claude, Grok, Gemini, Qwen, GLM) in exchange for anonymized usage data.
    29→
    30→**Already installed:** `bonsai` v0.3.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/bonsai`
    31→
    32→**Setup options:**
    33→
    34→### Option A: Per-session launch (recommended for testing)
    35→```bash
    36→bonsai start claude
    37→```
    38→
    39→### Option B: Project-level config (persistent)
    40→Add to `.claude/settings.local.json`:
    41→```json
    42→{
    43→  "env": {
    44→    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://go.trybons.ai",
    45→    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "<bonsai_api_key>"
    46→  }
    47→}
    48→```
    49→
    50→### Option C: Environment variables
    51→```bash
    52→ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://go.trybons.ai" ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<key>" claude
    53→```
    54→
    55→**Action required:** Run `bonsai login` to authenticate (GitHub OAuth).
    56→
    57→**Trade-off:** Anonymized data collection. Model names hidden (stealth mode). Use for dev/experimental sessions; keep direct Anthropic API for production/sensitive work.
    58→
    59→**Token savings:** 100% cost reduction on qualifying sessions.
    60→
    61→---
    62→
    63→## Layer 2: AI-Optimized Docs via Mintlify (reduce context loading)
    64→
    65→**What:** Turn local markdown docs into a searchable, AI-indexed documentation site with:
    66→- `llms.txt` — structured page index for LLM consumption
    67→- `llms-full.txt` — entire docs combined into one file
    68→- `skill.md` — capability summary telling agents what Rhea can do
    69→- **Hosted MCP server** — AI tools search docs on-demand instead of loading everything into context
    70→
    71→**Key insight from Mintlify docs:** "MCP servers don't consume context until the AI calls a search tool." This means lazy-loading instead of upfront file reads.
    72→
    73→### Setup
    74→```bash
    75→npx mintlify@latest init    # Initialize in docs/
    76→npx mintlify@latest dev     # Preview locally
    77→```
    78→
    79→### Create local `llms.txt` (immediate, no Mintlify needed)

0→# Rhea — Core Context Module
     1→> Reconstructed from origin conversations: eb53e82c, db9feb88, 72177dd4
     2→> Last updated: 2026-02-13
     3→
     4→## 1. Genesis — The Intellectual Chain
     5→
     6→### Origin Point
     7→**First message:** "Давай обсудим преимущества и недостатки григорианского календаря."
     8→*(Let's discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the Gregorian calendar.)*
     9→
    10→What began as a calendar critique became a deep excavation of how civilizations structure time, perception, and daily life — ultimately producing the Rhea project.
    11→
    12→### The Chain (each step emerged organically from the previous)
    13→
    14→1. **Gregorian calendar critique** → NOT for taxes, for Easter/equinox drift fix. Julian accumulated ~10 days of error. Editorial choices masked as objectivity.
    15→2. **Naive realism (когнитивное искажение)** → Recognition that calendar "neutrality" is itself a cognitive bias — all temporal systems encode power structures.
    16→3. **42 calendar systems catalogued** → Civil (Gregorian, ISO 8601, Unix epoch), Religious (Hijri, Hebrew, Buddhist, Hindu), Historical (Julian, Roman AUC, Mayan Long Count, Chinese Stem-Branch), Technical (TAI, GPS time). The user's own device revealed Hijri calendar (Sha'ban 25, 1447 AH) — infrastructure bias made visible.
    17→4. **Symbolic power mechanisms** → Calendars as governance tools:
    18→   - Chinese Mandate of Heaven (天命) — cosmic legitimacy
    19→   - Confucian Rectification of Names (正名) — who names reality, controls it
    20→   - Roman imperial cult — deified time (July, August)
    21→   - Gramsci's hegemony — manufactured consent through "common sense"
    22→   - Lukes' three dimensions of power — shaping preferences, not just decisions
    23→   - Bourdieu's doxa — unquestioned assumptions as invisible power
    24→5. **"They define not behavior but categories of thought"** → The deepest insight: cultural mechanisms don't control what you do, they control what you *can think*.
    25→6. **Health/longevity correlations** → Japanese gengo (era names) as philosophical markers, circadian rhythm research, cultural frameworks that produce measurable wellbeing differences.
    26→7. **Daily defaults as managed environment** → Every "elite" wellness ritual (cold exposure, fasting, circadian alignment, grounding) reconstructs what hunter-gatherers got for free. Modern life is a *managed deprivation* of ancestral defaults.
    27→8. **"Which aspects of my life are out of control for reasons I don't notice?"** → Personal pivot from theoretical to applied.
    28→9. **Polyvagal theory + ADHD + interoception** → Keywords crystallized: cognitive exceptions, parasympathetic system, vagus nerve, rigid structures, proprioception, spontaneity, anankastic disorder, ADHD. The body's regulatory systems as the missing link between cultural mechanisms and daily wellbeing.
    29→10. **Agent teams concept** → Multi-disciplinary AI system to reconstruct daily defaults using ALL available human knowledge.
    30→11. **Rhea — iOS app + scientific paper** → Two concrete deliverables: "Mathematics of Rhea" paper and AppStore app.
    31→
    32→## 2. Core Philosophical Framework
    33→
    34→### The Hunter-Gatherer Calibration Zero
    35→Every expensive wellness practice reconstructs what foragers received as environmental default:
    36→- **Cold exposure** (Wim Hof, cold plunges) → foragers had no central heating
    37→- **Intermittent fasting** → food wasn't available 24/7
    38→- **Grounding/earthing** → barefoot was default
    39→- **Circadian alignment** → no artificial light
    40→- **Movement variability** → no chairs, no static postures
    41→- **Social bonding rhythms** → tribal co-regulation, not isolated nuclear families
    42→
    43→**Principle:** If you have to pay for it, buy a device for it, or schedule it — it was probably free in the ancestral environment.
    44→
    45→### The 8-Level Symbolic Power Framework
    46→(Extracted from eb53e82c, synthesized across civilizations)
    47→
    48→| Level | Mechanism | Example |
    49→|-------|-----------|---------|
    50→| 1 | Time naming | Gregorian months, era names |
    51→| 2 | Cosmic legitimacy | Mandate of Heaven, divine right |
    52→| 3 | Linguistic control | Rectification of Names, Sapir-Whorf |
    53→| 4 | Category formation | What counts as "food", "work", "rest" |
    54→| 5 | Habitual infrastructure | When meals happen, when sleep "should" occur |
    55→| 6 | Hegemonic consent | Gramsci — internalized "common sense" |
    56→| 7 | Preference shaping | Lukes — you don't even want what you're missing |
    57→| 8 | Doxa | Bourdieu — unquestionable, invisible assumptions |
    58→
    59→### ADHD-Optimized Design Principle
    60→"If it works for ADHD — it works for everyone. Not the other way around."
    61→
    62→Rationale (validated via "curb cut effect"):
    63→- Executive dysfunction is the *default under stress*, not a minority condition
    64→- Passive profiling (behavioral signals) assumes executive dysfunction as baseline
    65→- All UX must work without requiring sustained voluntary attention
    66→- Gamification that helps ADHD may feel patronizing to others → adaptive, not one-size-fits-all
    67→
    68→### Circabidian / Ultradian / Infradian
    69→The 24-hour cycle is NOT the only temporal unit that matters:
    70→- **Ultradian** (~90-120 min): BRAC cycles, attention oscillation, REM cycling
    71→- **Circadian** (~24h): sleep-wake, cortisol, melatonin, body temperature
    72→- **Circabidian** (~48h): some immune and hormonal cycles operate on 2-day rhythms
    73→- **Infradian** (>24h): menstrual (~28d), seasonal (circannual), lunar influences on behavior
    74→
    75→**Key insight for ADHD:** Circabidian rhythms may explain why "good days" and "bad days" alternate — not random, but a 48-hour oscillation in dopaminergic/noradrenergic tone.
    76→
    77→## 3. The Polyvagal-Interoception Bridge
    78→
    79→From chat db9feb88 — the scientific foundation connecting cultural mechanisms to bodily experience:
    80→
    81→### Invisible Cultural Mechanisms Controlling Daily Life
    82→1. **Meal timing architecture** — when you eat shapes circadian gene expression (not just what you eat)
    83→2. **Posture ecology** — chairs, desks, cars create chronic flexion; ancestral default was squatting, varied surfaces
    84→3. **Light spectrum management** — artificial light suppresses melatonin 50-80% vs firelight
    85→4. **Social synchronization** — modern schedules desynchronize natural co-regulation rhythms
    86→5. **Temperature variability deprivation** — thermoneutral zones eliminate thermogenesis training
    87→6. **Sound environment** — constant low-frequency noise activates sympathetic nervous system
    88→
    89→### The Vagal Tone Connection
    90→- Polyvagal theory (Porges): three-tier autonomic hierarchy — ventral vagal (social engagement) → sympathetic (fight/flight) → dorsal vagal (freeze/shutdown)
    91→- **Interoception** = ability to sense internal body states → directly linked to emotional regulation
    92→- ADHD correlates with reduced interoceptive accuracy → explains alexithymia, emotional dysregulation
    93→- **Proprioception** feeds vagal tone → movement variability is not exercise, it's nervous system regulation
    94→
    95→### Anankastic Traits + ADHD Paradox
    96→The user identified a personal pattern: rigid structures (anankastic/OCPD traits) coexisting with ADHD spontaneity needs. This is not contradiction — it's *compensatory architecture*: the rigid structures exist BECAUSE executive function is unreliable, not despite it.
    97→
    98→**Design implication for Rhea:** The app must provide structure that feels like freedom, not constraint. Scaffolding that dissolves when not needed.
    99→

You are a Doc Extractor for the Rhea project. Create 2 files.

Context: Rhea is an agent coordination OS — not an app. Git-backed virtual office. Protocol: capsule → gems → incidents → decisions → procedures. Survives provider outages. 3 agents active (Rex/Opus, B2/Opus, GPT-5.2). Firebase real-time sync. 6 providers, 31 models, 4 cost tiers.

**1. /Users/sa/rh.1/docs/public/ONE_PAGER.md**
One page. Three sections: What / Why / How.
- What: Agent coordination OS. Git-backed. Protocol-driven. Provider-agnostic.
- Why: Multi-agent work has no memory, no reproducibility, no survival guarantees. Sessions die. Context is lost. Teams can't coordinate across terminals.

0→# Rhea Virtual Office
     1→> The coordination layer between all active agents
     2→> Created: 2026-02-16
     3→
     4→## Active Desks
     5→
     6→| Desk | Agent | Model | Terminal | Status | Current Task |
     7→|------|-------|-------|----------|--------|-------------|
     8→| LEAD | Opus 4.6 "братик" | claude-opus-4-6 | rh.1 | ALIVE | Office build |
     9→| B2 | B-2nd (restored) | claude-opus-4-6 | B-2nd | ALIVE | Self-reflection + GitHub auth |
    10→| GPT | ChatGPT 5.2 | gpt-5.2-thinking | ChatGPT app | ALIVE | Idea generation |
    11→| COWORK | Argos (Claude Opus 4.6) | claude-opus-4-6 | Cowork Desktop App | ALIVE | Cross-exchange + infra |
    12→| — | On-demand sonnet agents | claude-sonnet-4 | spawned by LEAD | IDLE | — |
    13→
    14→## Communication Protocol
    15→
    16→### Inbound (to office)
    17→Every agent drops results here:
    18→- `ops/virtual-office/inbox/` — raw dumps from any agent
    19→- Naming: `{DESK}_{timestamp}_{topic}.md`
    20→- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`
    21→
    22→### Outbound (from office)
    23→- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
    24→- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
    25→- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`
    26→
    27→### Shared State
    28→- `REDACTED.md` -- what matters right now (updated by LEAD)
    29→- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` -- things that broke + current status
    30→- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` -- ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
    31→- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` -- decisions made today with rationale
    32→
    33→## Data Flow
    34→
    35→```
    36→[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
    37→[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
    38→[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
    39→                                                     ↓
    40→                                            [outbox/ or git push]
    41→```
    42→
    43→## Rules
    44→1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
    45→2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
    46→3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) goes to GEMS.md immediately
    47→4. Every broken thing goes to INCIDENTS.md immediately
    48→5. Every decision goes to DECISIONS.md with "why" and "who decided"
    49→6. Git push at least every 30 minutes
    50→7. Every agent logs API calls to logs/bridge_calls.jsonl
    51→
    52→## Canonical Truth
    53→- BACKLOG.md (ops/BACKLOG.md) is the single source for all work items
    54→- TODAY_CAPSULE.md is the single source for "what matters now"
    55→- DECISIONS.md is the single source for "why we did X"
    56→- Git is the audit trail. If it is not committed, it did not happen.
    57→
    58→## Inbox/Outbox SLA
    59→- Inbox items processed by LEAD within 1 hour of discovery
    60→- Outbox tasks acknowledged by target desk within 2 hours
    61→- Stale items (> 4 h unprocessed) auto-escalate to INCIDENTS
    62→
    63→## Promotion Rules
    64→- Chat insight repeated 2x -- becomes a GEM (with ID)
    65→- GEM referenced 3x -- becomes a PROCEDURE (`docs/procedures/`)
    66→- PROCEDURE failing 2x -- becomes an INCIDENT
    67→- INCIDENT resolved + verified -- becomes a DECISION (what we learned)
    68→
    69→## Questions Gate (MANDATORY)
    70→- **No questions during execution.** Period.
    71→- Before any question, agent MUST have completed:
    72→  1. Extracted assumptions (labeled [ASSUMPTION])
    73→  2. Proposed plan
    74→  3. Produced draft outputs
    75→- All remaining questions (max 3) go in a single "Questions Gate" block at END of output
    76→- **Every question costs 1 artifact.** 1 question = 1 new file in inbox. No artifact, no question.
    77→
    78→## Defaults (eliminates need to ask)
    79→- Format not specified -- markdown, files in `ops/virtual-office/inbox/`

    14→## Communication Protocol
    15→
    16→### Inbound (to office)
    17→Every agent drops results here:
    18→- `ops/virtual-office/inbox/` — raw dumps from any agent
    19→- Naming: `{DESK}_{timestamp}_{topic}.md`
    20→- Example: `GPT_20260216_context-tax-collector.md`, `B2_20260216_self-reflection.md`
    21→
    22→### Outbound (from office)
    23→- `ops/virtual-office/outbox/` — tasks assigned to specific desks
    24→- Naming: `TO_{DESK}_{priority}_{topic}.md`
    25→- Example: `TO_B2_P1_fix-github-auth.md`
    26→
    27→### Shared State
    28→- `REDACTED.md` -- what matters right now (updated by LEAD)
    29→- `ops/virtual-office/INCIDENTS.md` -- things that broke + current status
    30→- `ops/virtual-office/GEMS.md` -- ideas, insights, quotes worth keeping
    31→- `ops/virtual-office/DECISIONS.md` -- decisions made today with rationale
    32→
    33→## Data Flow
    34→
    35→```
    36→[ChatGPT] ──ideas──→ [inbox/] ──LEAD routes──→ [agent task]
    37→[B-2nd]   ──results─→ [inbox/]                      ↓
    38→[Sonnet]  ──results─→ [inbox/]               [deliverable]
    39→                                                     ↓
    40→                                            [outbox/ or git push]
    41→```
    42→
    43→## Rules
    44→1. Every agent writes to inbox/, only LEAD reads and routes
    45→2. LEAD updates TODAY_CAPSULE at least every 2 hours
    46→3. Every external insight (ChatGPT, web, bridge) goes to GEMS.md immediately
    47→4. Every broken thing goes to INCIDENTS.md immediately
    48→5. Every decision goes to DECISIONS.md with "why" and "who decided"
    49→6. Git push at least every 30 minutes
    50→7. Every agent logs API calls to logs/bridge_calls.jsonl
    51→
    52→## Canonical Truth
    53→- BACKLOG.md (ops/BACKLOG.md) is the single source for all work items
    54→- TODAY_CAPSULE.md is the single source for "what matters now"
    55→- DECISIONS.md is the single source for "why we did X"
    56→- Git is the audit trail. If it is not committed, it did not happen.
    57→
    58→## Inbox/Outbox SLA
    59→- Inbox items processed by LEAD within 1 hour of discovery
    60→- Outbox tasks acknowledged by target desk within 2 hours
    61→- Stale items (> 4 h unprocessed) auto-escalate to INCIDENTS

    63→## Promotion Rules
    64→- Chat insight repeated 2x -- becomes a GEM (with ID)
    65→- GEM referenced 3x -- becomes a PROCEDURE (`docs/procedures/`)
    66→- PROCEDURE failing 2x -- becomes an INCIDENT
    67→- INCIDENT resolved + verified -- becomes a DECISION (what we learned)
    68→
    69→## Questions Gate (MANDATORY)
    70→- **No questions during execution.** Period.
    71→- Before any question, agent MUST have completed:
    72→  1. Extracted assumptions (labeled [ASSUMPTION])
    73→  2. Proposed plan
    74→  3. Produced draft outputs
    75→- All remaining questions (max 3) go in a single "Questions Gate" block at END of output
    76→- **Every question costs 1 artifact.** 1 question = 1 new file in inbox. No artifact, no question.
    77→
    78→## Defaults (eliminates need to ask)
    79→- Format not specified -- markdown, files in `ops/virtual-office/inbox/`
    80→- Priority not specified -- P0 stability, P1 context, P2 iOS, P3 community
    81→- Addressee not specified -- LEAD
    82→- Ambiguous -- produce A/B variants, deliver both to inbox
    83→- Info missing -- best-effort + [ASSUMPTION] tag
    84→

    86→- **No-output is failure.**
    87→- Every session MUST end with at least 1 artifact in inbox:
    88→  - BACKLOG.md updated, OR
    89→  - new PROCEDURE.md, OR
    90→  - new INCIDENT.md, OR
    91→  - updated TODAY_CAPSULE.md
    92→- Want to ask? Deliver artifact first, then ask.
    93→

0→# Why Multi-Provider AI Abstraction Beats Single Vendor Lock-In
     1→
     2→**ChatGPT Pro vs. Claude Cowork -- and why the real answer is neither alone**
     3→
     4→---
     5→
     6→## Introduction
     7→
     8→Two heavyweights now dominate the premium AI assistant market: OpenAI's ChatGPT Pro at $200/month and Anthropic's Claude Cowork, a desktop automation tool built into Claude Desktop. For technically literate professionals evaluating their AI tooling strategy, the choice is not obvious. Both promise to accelerate knowledge work, but they approach the problem from fundamentally different angles.
     9→
    10→This comparison examines pricing, capabilities, use cases, and limitations -- with special attention to why neither alone may be optimal for teams building sophisticated AI workflows.
    11→
    12→## What Each Product Is
    13→
    14→### ChatGPT Pro: Premium Reasoning at Scale
    15→
    16→ChatGPT Pro is OpenAI's top-tier subscription at $200/month, positioned for researchers, engineers, and professionals who use research-grade intelligence daily.
    17→
    18→Key features: unlimited access to o1 and o1-mini reasoning models, o1 Pro mode (a higher-compute version that "thinks harder and longer"), GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini, Advanced Voice Mode, Operator research preview (US-only) for autonomous web browsing, and extended Sora video generation access.
    19→
    20→Fundamentally, it is a subscription to compute-intensive reasoning, bundled with OpenAI's broader model suite.
    21→
    22→### Claude Cowork: Desktop Automation for Knowledge Workers
    23→
    24→Claude Cowork is a research preview available through Claude Desktop, included with Claude Pro ($20/month) and other paid subscriptions. Unlike ChatGPT Pro, Cowork is not a separate subscription tier -- it is an agentic capability layer that turns Claude into a multi-step task executor.
    25→
    26→Core capabilities: local file handling (read, analyze, create, and modify docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf), multi-step task planning and execution, virtual machine sandboxing, MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration with 500+ external tools, parallel workstream coordination, and a plugin ecosystem with 11 production plugins spanning sales, legal, finance, marketing, data analysis, and software development.
    27→
    28→## Pricing and Access Models
    29→
    30→| Aspect | ChatGPT Pro | Claude Pro | Claude Max 5x | Claude Max 20x |
    31→|--------|------------|-----------|---------------|----------------|
    32→| Monthly Cost | $200 | $20 | $100 | $200 |
    33→| Reasoning Model | o1, o1 Pro | Opus 4.6 | Opus 4.6 | Opus 4.6 |
    34→| Cowork Access | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
    35→| Browser Automation | Operator (US only) | Via MCP | Via MCP | Via MCP |
    36→| Message Limits | High | High | Very high | Maximum (20x) |
    37→
    38→The math favors Claude: a Pro user ($20/month) gets full Cowork access with 100+ MCP connectors at 1/10th the cost. Claude Max 5x ($100) provides 2x--5x higher capacity at half the price. Claude Max 20x ($200) matches ChatGPT Pro's cost while adding Cowork, superior file handling, and broader tool integration.
    39→
    40→## Core Capabilities Comparison
    41→
    42→### Reasoning Depth: o1 Pro vs. Opus 4.6
    43→
    44→This is ChatGPT Pro's primary competitive advantage. o1 Pro mode produces more reliably accurate responses for data science, programming, and case-law analysis. It excels at mathematical proofs, multi-step scientific problem-solving, competitive programming, and legal reasoning.
    45→
    46→Claude Opus 4.6, released in February 2026, shipped with major upgrades but lacks the explicit chain-of-thought reasoning that characterizes o1. For pure reasoning complexity, o1 Pro holds a legitimate edge.
    47→
    48→**Verdict**: ChatGPT Pro wins for pure reasoning; Claude wins for practical knowledge work.
    49→
    50→### Tool Use and File Handling
    51→
    52→ChatGPT Pro offers browser automation via Operator (research preview, US only, rate-limited), limited file creation, and no direct file-system access. Claude Cowork provides native local file-system read/write for all document types, professional document formatting, 500+ external tool integrations via MCP, agentic multi-tool workflow orchestration, and 11 production plugins.
    53→
    54→**Verdict**: Claude Cowork dominates for automation, file management, and tool orchestration.
    55→
    56→### MCP Support
    57→
    58→The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that creates secure, two-way connections between AI systems and external data sources. MCP is native to Claude's architecture; ChatGPT does not support it.
    59→
    60→Benefits: hundreds of community-built integrations, private database connections, bidirectional communication, and a standardized interface across Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Claude for Work.
    61→
